gaps.sentence: The bank makes no ___ for using its cash machines.
gaps.hint: money asked for a service; pattern: make a ___ for
gaps.explanation: 'Make a charge for something' means to ask payment for a service; 'tip' is extra money for good service.

gaps.sentence: He gave a ___ summary of the 40-page report.
gaps.explanation: 'A brief summary' — adjective; 'briefly' is the adverb.

gaps.sentence: After graduating he struggled to find ___ for several months.
gaps.explanation: 'Work' is uncountable, so it fits after 'find' with no article; 'job' would need 'a job'.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ your application at its May meeting.
gaps.explanation: The finite verb slot needs 'consider'; 'considerable' means large.

gaps.sentence: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon yesterday.
gaps.explanation: 'Lay' is the past of 'lie' (recline): he lay on the sofa. 'Laid' would need an object.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.
